title.zh: 气血养颜：气血充足才能容光焕发
title.en: Qi-Blood Beauty: Radiance from Sufficient Qi & Blood

description.zh: 气血是美容的根本，掌握气血养颜的方法，让面色红润、皮肤润泽
description.en: Qi-Blood is the foundation of beauty, master methods for radiant complexion

zh.text: 《黄帝内经》有言："气血不和，百病乃变化而生。"在中医看来，气血是生命的根本物质。气为血之帅，推动血液运行于全身经脉；血为气之母，承载并滋养着气。气血充足调和的人，面色必然红润有光泽，皮肤润泽饱满，精神充沛。反之，气血亏虚则面色萎黄、皮肤干燥、毛发枯槁，衰老的迹象也会提早出现。所以，想要容光焕发，必须从调理气血这个根本入手。
气血与美容的关系
气和血虽然功能不同，但两者密不可分。气属阳，主动，具有推动、温煦、防御、固摄的作用；血属阴，主静，具有滋养、濡润的功能。气将血液输送到头面部的皮肤毛窍，血则带来营养物质滋润肌肤。只有气血调和，面部才能获得充足的营养，呈现出健康的色泽和弹性。
气的作用
在美容层面，气的功能主要体现在四个方面：一是推动作用，气能将血液输送到面部皮肤，如果气虚推动无力，面部就会苍白无华；二是温煦作用，气维持肌肤的正常温度，气虚则手足不温、面部发凉；三是防御作用，卫气布散于体表，抵御外邪侵袭，气虚的人皮肤屏障功能减弱，容易过敏、感染；四是固摄作用，气能固摄津液，防止过度流失，气虚则自汗多汗，皮肤水分流失加快，容易干燥。
血的作用
血对美容的重要性更是不言而喻。血液中携带的营养物质是面部肌肤的直接"食粮"。血充足则面色红润、皮肤饱满有弹性；血虚则面色萎黄、皮肤干瘪、容易出现皱纹。我在临床中接触过不少因节食减肥导致月经量少、面色晦暗的年轻女性，追问之下大多有过度节食的经历——脾胃受损，气血生化无源，面部自然失去了光彩。
气血不足的表现
在临床上，气虚和血虚往往同时出现，但二者的表现各有侧重，需要仔细辨别。
气虚的表现
气虚的人最典型的特征就是"累"——说话声音低弱，稍微活动就气喘吁吁，整天觉得疲乏无力。在容貌上，面色要么苍白如纸，要么萎黄无光；皮肤松弛下垂，缺乏紧致感；稍微一动就出虚汗，免疫力差，容易感冒。这些都是气不足以固摄和推动的表现。
血虚的表现
血虚的人则更多表现为"干"和"淡"。面色萎黄或淡白无华，嘴唇和指甲颜色淡白；经常头晕眼花，蹲下起来时眼前发黑；心悸失眠，睡眠浅、多梦；皮肤干燥起屑，头发干枯易断、稀疏脱落。女性还会出现月经量少、颜色淡、周期延后等问题。《难经》中提到的"血主濡之"，指的就是血的滋润营养功能，血虚则濡养不足，全身各处都会出现"干"的信号。
补气养颜方法
补气的方法很多，但最平易近人的莫过于饮食调理和穴位按摩。在临床上，我通常会从这两个方面给患者建议。
补气食物
黄芪是补气的代表药物，有"补气之长"之称，能升阳举陷、益卫固表。日常可以用黄芪泡水或煲汤，与鸡肉同炖效果更佳。党参性质平和，善补中益气，适合体质偏弱、容易疲劳的人。山药补脾益气，同时能滋养肺肾，是药食同源的佳品。红枣补气养血、药性甘温，是日常养生的首选。鸡肉则能温中补气，尤其适合产后或病后体虚的人。
补气穴位
足三里是补中益气的第一要穴，位于膝盖外侧凹陷下三寸处，每天按揉5分钟，能健运脾胃、补益气血。气海穴位于肚脐下1.5寸，是元气汇聚之处，按摩或艾灸此穴都能培补元气。关元穴在肚脐下3寸，是男子藏精、女子蓄血之处，对提升整体阳气很有帮助。脾俞穴位于背部，是脾的背俞穴，按摩此穴可以健脾益气。
补血养颜方法
补血食物
当归被誉为"补血第一药"，既能补血又能活血，是四物汤的君药。阿胶是驴皮熬制而成，补血滋阴效果显著，尤其适合血虚导致的皮肤干燥、面色萎黄。桂圆补心脾、益气血，适合心神不宁、失眠多梦的血虚者。黑芝麻补肝肾、益精血，长期食用能使头发乌黑亮泽。菠菜含铁量丰富，中医认为其性凉味甘，能养血润燥，适合血虚便秘者。
补血穴位
血海穴是补血养血的要穴，位于大腿内侧，髌骨内上缘上2寸处。每天按揉此穴，能促进血液循环、改善面色。三阴交是肝、脾、肾三条阴经的交会穴，位于内踝尖上3寸，是调理气血的重要穴位。肝俞穴能养肝补血，肝藏血，肝血充足则面色红润。膈俞穴被称为"血会"，是治疗血证的要穴，对于血虚或血瘀都有调理作用。
气血双补经典方
四物汤
四物汤由当归、熟地黄、白芍、川芎四味药组成，是中医补血养血的经典方剂，被誉为"妇科第一方""女人养血第一方"。其中当归补血活血，熟地黄滋阴补血，白芍养血柔肝，川芎活血行气。四药合用，补而不滞，滋而不腻，最适合血虚而兼有血瘀的人群。我在临床上常用此方加减调理月经不调、面色萎黄等症。
八珍汤
八珍汤是四物汤与四君子汤的合方，包含了补气的四君子（人参、白术、茯苓、甘草）和补血的四物（当归、熟地、白芍、川芎），是气血双补的代表方。适合气血两虚、面色苍白或萎黄、头晕乏力、气短心悸的人群。现代人工作压力大、饮食不规律，气血两虚的情况非常普遍，八珍汤是临床上使用频率极高的方剂之一。

zh.title: 当归黄芪养颜汤
zh.instructions:
1. 鸡肉切块焯水
2. 当归、黄芪洗净
3. 所有材料放入炖盅
4. 炖煮1.5小时
5. 温服，每周2-3次
6. 补气养血，改善面色

zh.text: 日常养颜习惯
除了饮食和穴位调理，日常的生活习惯对气血的影响同样不可忽视。熬夜是耗伤气血最大的元凶之一，夜间是气血回归脏腑、进行修复的时间，长期熬夜等于让气血一直处于"透支"状态。适度运动能促进气血运行，但切忌过度——大汗淋漓会耗气伤津。情绪方面，过度的思虑和忧虑都会暗耗气血，保持心情舒畅本身就是一种补养。饮食上要注意均衡营养，不偏食、不过度节食，脾胃得养，气血自然源源不断地化生。
温馨提示：气血养颜需要循序渐进，不可急于求成。严重气血不足者应在中医师指导下进行调理，配合汤药治疗，通常坚持调理一到三个月就能看到明显改善。

en.text: The Huangdi Neijing states: "When Qi and Blood are disharmonious, all diseases arise." In TCM, Qi and Blood are the fundamental substances of life. Qi commands Blood, driving circulation through the meridians; Blood nourishes Qi, serving as its carrier. Those with harmonious, sufficient Qi-Blood naturally have a rosy, glowing complexion, moist and supple skin, and abundant energy. Conversely, Qi-Blood deficiency leads to sallow complexion, dry skin, withered hair, and premature aging. Therefore, true radiance begins with regulating Qi and Blood — the very foundation of beauty.
Qi-Blood & Beauty Relationship

Although Qi and Blood have different functions, they are inseparable. Qi belongs to Yang, governs movement, and provides propulsion, warming, defense, and retention. Blood belongs to Yin, governs stillness, and provides nourishment and moisture. Qi delivers Blood to the skin and pores of the face, while Blood brings nutrients to moisturize the skin. Only when Qi and Blood are harmonized can the face receive adequate nourishment, displaying healthy color and elasticity.
Functions of Qi

From a beauty perspective, Qi has four main functions. First, propulsion — Qi drives Blood to the facial skin; when Qi is deficient, circulation is weak, resulting in a pale complexion. Second, warming — Qi maintains normal skin temperature; Qi deficiency leads to cold hands and feet and a cool facial temperature. Third, defense — defensive Qi spreads over the body surface to ward off external pathogens; those with Qi deficiency have weakened skin barrier function, making them prone to allergies and infections. Fourth, retention — Qi retains fluids to prevent excessive loss; Qi deficiency causes spontaneous sweating and accelerated moisture loss from the skin, leading to dryness.
Functions of Blood

Blood's importance to beauty is self-evident. The nutrients carried in the blood are the direct "food" for facial skin. Sufficient blood gives a rosy complexion and plump, elastic skin; blood deficiency causes a sallow complexion, wrinkled, lax skin. In my clinical practice, I have encountered many young women who developed scanty menstruation and dull complexions after extreme dieting — their spleen and stomach were damaged, the source of Qi-Blood production was cut off, and their faces naturally lost their luster.
Signs of Qi-Blood Deficiency
In clinical practice, Qi deficiency and Blood deficiency often coexist, but their presentations differ and require careful differentiation.
Qi Deficiency Signs

The most characteristic feature of Qi deficiency is "fatigue" — a weak voice, shortness of breath after minimal activity, and a pervasive sense of tiredness. Facially, the complexion is either pale as paper or sallow and lusterless; the skin appears loose and sagging, lacking firmness. There may be spontaneous sweating upon slight movement, weakened immunity, and frequent colds. These are all manifestations of Qi being insufficient to retain and propel.
Blood Deficiency Signs

Blood deficiency manifests more as "dryness" and "paleness." The complexion appears sallow or pale white; lips and nail beds are pale in color. Common symptoms include frequent dizziness, blurred vision, darkening before the eyes when standing up, palpitations, insomnia with light sleep and excessive dreaming, dry and flaky skin, and brittle, thinning hair. Women may experience scanty, pale menstruation with delayed cycles. The Nan Jing (Classic of Difficulties) states: "Blood governs moistening" — blood deficiency leads to insufficient nourishment, and the whole body sends signals of "dryness."
Qi-Tonifying Beauty Methods
There are many ways to tonify Qi, but the most accessible are dietary therapy and acupoint massage. In clinical practice, I usually recommend these two approaches to patients.
Qi-Tonifying Foods

Astragalus (Huang Qi) is the representative Qi-tonifying herb, known as the "chief of Qi tonics." It raises Yang, secures the exterior, and strengthens the defensive Qi. It can be steeped in hot water as a tea or simmered in soup, especially with chicken. Codonopsis (Dang Shen) is mild in nature, excels at tonifying middle Qi, and suits those with weak constitutions and easy fatigue. Yam (Shan Yao) tonifies spleen Qi while also nourishing the lung and kidney — a truly versatile food-medicine. Red dates (Hong Zao) tonify Qi and Blood with a sweet, warm nature, making them a top choice for daily health. Chicken warms the middle and tonifies Qi, particularly suitable for postpartum or post-illness recovery.
Qi-Tonifying Acupoints

Zusanli (ST36) is the foremost acupoint for tonifying middle Qi. Located four finger-widths below the knee, lateral to the shinbone, daily massage for five minutes strengthens the spleen-stomach and supplements Qi and Blood. Qihai (CV6), located 1.5 cun below the navel, is where original Qi gathers; massage or moxibustion here can tonify the source of Qi. Guanyuan (CV4), 3 cun below the navel, stores essence in men and houses blood in women, greatly assisting in elevating Yang Qi. Pishu (BL20), on the back, is the back-shu point of the spleen; massaging it strengthens the spleen and tonifies Qi.
Blood-Tonifying Beauty Methods
Blood-Tonifying Foods

Angelica (Dang Gui) is hailed as the "primary blood-tonifying herb," capable of both tonifying and activating blood — it serves as the sovereign herb in the classic Four Substances Decoction. Donkey-hide gelatin (E Jiao), made from boiled donkey hide, significantly tonifies blood and nourishes Yin, especially suitable for blood deficiency manifesting as dry skin and sallow complexion. Longan (Gui Yuan) tonifies the heart and spleen, benefits Qi and Blood, and is excellent for those with palpitations and insomnia from blood deficiency. Black sesame (Hei Zhi Ma) tonifies the liver and kidney, benefits essence and blood, and with long-term consumption promotes glossy black hair. Spinach, rich in iron, is considered by TCM to cool the blood and moisten dryness, suitable for those with blood deficiency and constipation.
Blood-Tonifying Acupoints

Xuehai (SP10), located 2 cun above the upper-inner border of the patella, is the key acupoint for tonifying and nourishing blood. Daily massage here promotes blood circulation and improves complexion. Sanyinjiao (SP6), 3 cun above the medial malleolus, is the crossing point of the liver, spleen, and kidney meridians — an essential point for regulating Qi and Blood. Ganshu (BL18) nourishes the liver and tonifies blood; since the liver stores blood, sufficient liver blood gives a rosy complexion. Geshu (BL17), known as the "meeting point of blood," is important for treating both blood deficiency and blood stasis.
Classic Qi-Blood Tonifying Formulas
Four Substances Decoction (Si Wu Tang)

Si Wu Tang, composed of Angelica, Prepared Rehmannia, White Peony, and Chuanxiong, is the classic blood-tonifying formula of TCM, known as the "primary woman's formula" and "woman's first blood-nourishing formula." Angelica tonifies and activates blood, Prepared Rehmannia nourishes Yin and blood, White Peony nourishes blood and softens the liver, and Chuanxiong activates blood and moves Qi. The four herbs work together to tonify without causing stagnation and nourish without being greasy — ideal for those with blood deficiency accompanied by blood stasis. I frequently use this formula with modifications for irregular menstruation and sallow complexion.
Eight Treasures Decoction (Ba Zhen Tang)

Ba Zhen Tang combines Si Wu Tang with the Four Gentlemen Decoction (Ren Shen, Bai Zhu, Fu Ling, Gan Cao), making it the representative formula for simultaneously tonifying both Qi and Blood. It suits those with dual Qi-Blood deficiency presenting with pale or sallow complexion, dizziness, fatigue, shortness of breath, and palpitations. Given the high prevalence of Qi-Blood deficiency among modern people under work stress and irregular diets, Ba Zhen Tang is one of the most frequently prescribed formulas in clinical practice.

en.title: Angelica Astragalus Beauty Soup
en.instructions:
1. Cut chicken, blanch
2. Wash angelica and astragalus
3. Place all in stewing pot
4. Stew for 1.5 hours
5. Serve warm, 2-3 times weekly
6. Tonifies Qi-Blood, improves complexion

en.text: Daily Beauty Habits

Beyond dietary therapy and acupoint massage, daily lifestyle habits impact Qi and Blood just as significantly. Staying up late is one of the biggest drains on Qi and Blood — nighttime is when Qi and Blood return to the organs for repair, and chronic sleep deprivation keeps them in a constant state of depletion. Moderate exercise promotes Qi-Blood circulation, but overexertion must be avoided — profuse sweating damages both Qi and fluids. Emotionally, excessive worry and rumination silently consume Qi and Blood; maintaining a cheerful disposition is itself a form of nourishment. Diet should be nutritionally balanced without bias or extreme restriction — when the spleen and stomach are well-nourished, Qi and Blood are continuously generated.

Note: Qi-Blood beauty requires gradual progress. Those with severe deficiency should seek guidance from a qualified TCM practitioner. With proper treatment, visible improvement typically appears within one to three months of consistent regulation.
